_comment: Root certificates Windows is entitled to trust, by thumbprint. Read by engine/Phases-1.ps1 phase 39 (loaded in Scythe-V23.ps1 as $TRUSTED_ROOTS) to decide whether a certificate found in Cert:\LocalMachine\Root or Cert:\CurrentUser\Root got there legitimately. 'program' is the Microsoft Trusted Root Program participant list published through the CCADB (every root Windows will auto-install from the CTL; 'status' Included = trusted, Disabled = distrusted by Microsoft, NotBefore = trusted only for certificates issued before a cutoff). 'windows_shipped' is the small set of Microsoft's own roots that ship inside Windows rather than through the CTL, verified against https://www.microsoft.com/pkiops/docs/repository.htm. A root that is in neither list and not in the machine's AuthRoot store is reported by phase 39 as POSSIBLE for review; a root in 'program' with status Disabled is reported too. NOT a malware signature file. Regenerate with tools/Update-TrustedRoots.ps1 - do not hand-edit 'program'.

_comment_windows_shipped_legacy: Four more roots Windows ships and Microsoft's KB 293781 lists as required, but publishes only by subject and serial number, not thumbprint. All four expired between 1999 and 2020, and an expired root cannot validate anything signed after its expiry, so phase 39 recognises them by exact subject CN + serial AND requires NotAfter before expires_before. A cert that reuses the name but is still valid does not qualify and is reported for review.
